title: Shape the mood editor
question: Same Soundscape visual language, three different ways to build and fine-tune a 3–6-layer mood. Choose the working layout; the next step is a concise scope confirmation before the clickable prototype.

options.label: Layer board + inspector
options.thesis: See the whole atmosphere as a small board of sound layers; fine-tune one without losing the mix.
options.viewport: Scene navigation across the top; selected mood artwork and name at left above a 2×3 layer board; a right inspector exposes pan, fades, and playback for the selected layer; preview and save stay visible.
options.risk: Comparing detailed pan and fade values across layers takes selection; the board must not become decorative cards.

options.label: Listening field
options.thesis: Tune a conventional layer list while a stereo field shows where every sound sits in the atmosphere.
options.viewport: A focused mood header leads into a compact layer list at left and a wide stereo-position overview at right; volume and pan remain standard sliders, with selected-layer fades beneath the field.
options.risk: The field helps with placement, but could consume space better spent on ordinary editing; it must never imply surround sound or a game map.

options.label: Mood shelf + layer sheet
options.thesis: Keep the scene’s moods in a shallow art shelf, then give the selected mix a full-width, directly editable layer sheet.
options.viewport: A shallow horizontal shelf shows sibling moods; the selected mood opens beneath it as five aligned layer rows with volume, pan, loop, and fades in place; a fixed lower preview bar keeps auditioning close.
options.risk: Fast comparison and editing, but denser and more spreadsheet-like; the shelf must not shrink the 3–6-layer workspace.
